clue.text: Group meeting gets silly message full of bunkum mostly

indicators.note: full of means the anagram is stuffed with the next piece placed inside it
silly suggests the letters of message are scrambled into a new order
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: bunkum is nonsense, blah

explanation.surface: Someone at a gathering receives a daft note that is mostly nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' scrambles the fodder and 'mostly' docks the last letter of the nonsense word before it goes inside; 'Group meeting' looks like the setting but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a gathering of people, which is what a group meeting amounts to.

clue.text: Close building sealing ends off

indicators.note: the ends being sealed off means the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: building, as in making something

explanation.surface: A building nearby has its ends sealed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sealing ends off' strips M and G from MAKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Close in the sense of related or similar: kindred things are near each other in nature.

clue.text: Fancy marketing point being introduced by school!

indicators.note: being introduced by means the first piece is put into the middle of the next

parts.note: a school of thought is a sect
USP is a unique selling point in marketing

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a sales pitch being brought in by a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to imagine or believe it likely, the verb sense of suspect.

clue.text: Wizard about to assist diplomat in journey after cracking bubbly?

indicators.note: about means the wizard's word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a mage is a wizard
to assist is to aid
an envoy is a diplomat

explanation.surface: A wizard helps a diplomat on a trip that begins with champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the wizard wrap the rest after its first letter. A ship's first voyage starts by breaking a bottle of champagne over the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's first voyage traditionally follows a launch in which champagne is broken against the hull.

clue.text: Type to make place desert ultimately?

definitions.text: Type to make place desert ultimately?

parts.note: locus is Latin for place, used in English too

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter of the word desert

explanation.surface: Asks what sort of creature would turn a place into desert in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCUS plus T, the last letter of desert; swarms of these insects strip land bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming insects of this kind devour crops and vegetation, leaving land like a desert.

clue.text: Frenchman turning up in sombre attire or something naturally colourful?

indicators.note: in means the reversed name sits inside the colour word

parts.note: grey is a sombre colour of clothing

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman shows up dressed in drab clothes, or something brighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses the name in this down clue, and 'in' sets it inside the drab colour; the question mark flags the playful definition of plant life.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage and plants are naturally coloured green, so vegetation fits the cryptic description.

clue.text: Act as boxer returning blows

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: raps are blows or knocks

explanation.surface: A boxer hitting back in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns RAPS around.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers practise against partners, which is sparring.

clue.text: Figure "dead parrot" is being broadcast?

indicators.note: being broadcast means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: Polly is a stock parrot's name, and a dead one is Polly gone

explanation.surface: A figure of speech for a dead parrot goes out on air, recalling a comedy sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly is the classic name for a pet parrot; 'Polly gone' said out loud gives the shape word.
explanation.definitionFit: A many-sided plane shape is a geometrical figure.

clue.text: Surprisingly alive, tries to get going again

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters of the next words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone unexpectedly still breathing makes efforts to restart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges ALIVE TRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To revive or restore energy is to get something going again.

clue.text: Laughing like one who's just had an op?

definitions.text: like one who's just had an op?
definitions.meaning: after surgery a wound is closed with stitches

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means laughing uncontrollably, and literally describes a patient whose wound has been sewn up.

clue.text: European saint needing small room

parts.note: lav, short for lavatory, is the smallest room

explanation.surface: A saint who needs a little room.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavs are a group of peoples of eastern and central Europe.

clue.text: Plant in which eight birds nested according to Lear

definitions.meaning: a wild clematis with feathery seed heads

definitions.text: in which eight birds nested according to Lear
definitions.meaning: Edward Lear's limerick about an old man whose beard held two owls, a hen, four larks and a wren

explanation.definitionFit: The wild clematis is named for its fluffy seeds, and Lear's limerick has eight birds nesting in such whiskers.

clue.text: Source of illumination that's carried by Arbroath gillie

definitions.text: Source of illumination that's carried by Arbroath gillie

parts.words: Source of illumination that's carried by Arbroath gillie
parts.note: read Arbroath gillie and the run THGIL appears, the lamp word turned around

explanation.walkthrough: In 'arbroaTH GILlie' the letters T-H-G-I-L spell a lamp word backwards, so it carries that word reversing. A gillie is a Scottish hunting or fishing attendant; Arbroath is a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the white lamp on a vehicle's rear that comes on when it backs up.

clue.text: What could be permeating as the result of soak

indicators.note: could be says the letters of permeating can be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Something seeping through after a good drenching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges PERMEATING.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate or steep something thoroughly with a liquid is to soak it.

clue.text: Inspiration in test leading to one day of victory

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles
I is the Roman numeral one
VE Day was Victory in Europe day, 1945

explanation.surface: Encouragement found in an exam that leads to a triumphant day.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason or driving incentive is what inspires someone to act.

clue.text: Cold Italian city getting rid of one gangster and another?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: getting rid of means a letter is removed from the city

parts.note: Rimini is a resort city in Italy
I is the Roman numeral one
another gangster is Al Capone, known as Al

explanation.surface: A chilly Italian town gets rid of one mobster and then another.
explanation.walkthrough: Rimini loses one I to give RIMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a lawbreaker, a member of the underworld.

clue.text: Literary extracts a voter read out

indicators.note: read out means the words are spoken and their sound is used

parts.note: a voter is an elector

explanation.surface: Passages from books are read aloud by someone in the electorate.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic accent, 'an elector' sounds like the plural for collected excerpts.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin plural for collected passages or selections from authors.

clue.text: Communicating from phone outside university after revolution

indicators.note: outside means the phone word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to ring is to phone

indicators.note: after revolution means the university's name is turned backwards

parts.note: Yale is an American university

explanation.surface: Calling from a phone outside a campus after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' turns the US university backwards and 'outside' wraps the phone word around it; 'revolution' tempts as an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaying a message means passing it on, a form of communicating.

clue.text: Garment-fat bit of body must squeeze up in

indicators.note: squeeze in tells us to push one piece inside another
in completes the squeeze in instruction for placing the piece inside

parts.note: lard is fat

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the piece is read backwards

parts.note: a toe is a small part of the body

explanation.surface: A garment made of fat that a body part has to be squeezed into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the body part in this down clue and 'must squeeze ... in' places it inside the fat; the hyphen hides that the definition ends at Garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting one-piece costume worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Hostile feeling a part of the kingdom must cut down

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

indicators.note: cut down means the final letter is chopped off

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Resentment as one region of the realm has to make reductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims MUST to MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is animosity or ill will towards someone.

clue.text: Revolutionary member of Catholic congregation carries the cross

indicators.note: carries means one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a Marist belongs to the Society of Mary, a Catholic order
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A radical churchgoer bears the cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' has the religious order member hold the cross letter; Marists belong to the Society of Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Karl Marx favours revolution to overthrow capitalism.

clue.text: Protect home? No problem

parts.note: in means at home
sure is a casual way of saying no problem

explanation.surface: Asks whether to safeguard a house, and gets a breezy yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out a policy against loss is to protect oneself financially.

clue.text: Sure, any blogger can knock a party leader

indicators.note: knock suggests the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A blogger is free to criticise a political leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock' rearranges SURE ANY BLOGGER. He led the British Labour Party in the early 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: He was leader of the British Labour Party from 1932 to 1935.

clue.text: Conservative statesman's thick skin

definitions.meaning: Sir Robert ..., Tory prime minister and founder of the Metropolitan Police
the rind of fruit such as orange

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Peel was a Conservative prime minister, and the outer rind of a fruit has the same name.

clue.text: A sailor holding one end of harpoon?

definitions.text: A sailor holding one end of harpoon?

indicators.note: holding means the pair of pieces wrap around the letter

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: one end of picks the first letter of harpoon

explanation.surface: A seaman gripping the butt of a harpoon.
explanation.walkthrough: H from harpoon goes between A and AB. Captain Ahab hunts the whale in Melville's Moby-Dick.
explanation.definitionFit: The harpoon-wielding captain of Moby-Dick is the seafarer meant.

clue.text: Bringing a charge in case

definitions.meaning: accusing someone, the adjective of accusation
the grammatical case of a verb's direct object

explanation.definitionFit: The word means making an accusation, and is also the grammatical case for a direct object.

clue.text: Twist head off children's beloved toy

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a teddy bear is a child's favourite soft toy

explanation.surface: Wrench the head off a child's treasured teddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' removes T from TEDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A swirl of water or air turning in a circle is a twist of current.

clue.text: Lead actor's playing in priestly role

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about into a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive's s counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: The star performer is cast as a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges LEAD ACTORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacerdotal means relating to priests and their office.
